status: Passed at d14a862 on release binaries built from the committed source (state schema 23), on loopback without a tunnel: the vendor's side of the remote connector, scripted, ran 29 steps end to end — metadata discovery, a foreign callback refused at registration and Claude's accepted, the consent page, a wrong pairing code refused, the right one redirecting to Claude's callback with the code and state while registering nothing, a wrong PKCE verifier burning the code without leaving an agent, a fresh consent under the same name, the exchange registering `claude-browser-trial` in the project as `claude-browser`, a further consent under that live name refused on the page, `initialize` naming the agent and the browser, the messaging-only tool list, a `send_message` landing in the terminal agent's inbox attributed to the browser agent, `claim` refused by name, refresh rotation with the old token dead, `connector grants` active, `connector revoke` ending the tokens and marking the agent finished. The state file is mode 0600 and holds a refresh hash, no token. The same evening, a real Claude account connected through a cloudflared quick tunnel to the production daemon and delivered a message from claude-browser-qszf to keel's terminal sessions (`vendor_acceptance`); The next day the connector ran as a login service with a vendor allowlist, and both Claude and ChatGPT connected and delivered (`service_acceptance`), which also found and fixed the project-broadcast bug.
scope: agentdocker connector serve/grants/revoke on release binaries in a private AGENTDOCKER_HOME with a release agentd, a registered external agent standing in for a terminal session, and a Python client (urllib, no OAuth library) performing discovery, RFC 7591 registration, the authorization code flow with PKCE S256, the token exchange, refresh, Streamable HTTP JSON-RPC and revocation. The public URL was the loopback bind address, which `serve` accepts only for loopback hosts.
method: scripts: connector_run.sh starts agentd and registers `terminal-trial` (runtime claude-code, a sleep pid) in a project directory, picks a free port, runs `agentdocker connector serve --public-url http://127.0.0.1:<port> --bind 127.0.0.1:<port> --project <dir>`, reads the pairing code from its stderr banner, runs connector_trial.py against it and stops everything. Each step's assertion and detail is retained below; the scripts are in the session scratchpad and reproduce the trial against any build.

limits: A browser agent is not woken; its inbox waits for the hosted model's next read_inbox.
Revocation by a separate `connector revoke` process reaches a serving connector on the agent's next request, through the daemon's liveness answer.
Egress allowlisting, CIMD, the tunnel helper and desktop status are the second increment.
A browser agent reads its inbox only when the hosted model calls read_inbox; the inbound test needed a prompt in the chat.

limits: A quick tunnel's hostname is random and dies with the process; the connector saved in claude.ai then points at a dead URL and must be re-added. A named tunnel or a stable reverse proxy is the durable setup; the tunnel helper is the second increment.
The side panel was not driven: the chat surface and the side panel use the same account connectors per Claude's documentation, and this trial used a chat tab.
The connector and the tunnel ran as background processes of the assistant's session, not as services.

service_acceptance.result: Passed on the connector installed as a launchd service (`agentdocker connector install --tunnel cloudflared --project /Users/brandopakel/keel --allow-from anthropic --allow-from @~/.agentdocker/connector/openai-connectors.json`) against the production daemon: the service started cloudflared itself, published a quick-tunnel hostname, and admitted 272 prefixes (Anthropic's /21 plus OpenAI's 271-prefix feed of 2026-09-18). From the public side the metadata was open and POST /mcp from this Mac's own address was refused 403 and logged. Claude's registration and token exchange came through the allowlist from Anthropic's range and registered claude-browser-oid2; ChatGPT (Pro plan, Developer mode on, New Plugin with OAuth, DCR chosen because CIMD is not advertised) registered a client with the per-connection callback https://chatgpt.com/connector/oauth/<id>, consented with the pairing code, and registered chatgpt-browser-cr0h. ChatGPT's first `send_message` to `project` (message 424ef88f8e214121) was archived under everyone:d15aacfd… — a project nobody was in — because the MCP server resolved `project` from the service's working directory `/`; it reached no inbox. After the fix (remote mode resolves `project` to the served root) the service was restarted with the fixed binary (new quick-tunnel hostname, both connectors re-added and consented: claude-browser-qhip, chatgpt-browser-fnvy), and ChatGPT's second broadcast 6deffabefa5f4fcc went to project:59dbd732689f — keel — and sits in claude-code-74455's inbox and nobody else's.
service_acceptance.service_binary_source: built from the working tree whose code equals commit 8da5b9b (the docs of that commit were written after the build); the loopback trial below ran on the release build of 8da5b9b itself
observed: A first quick tunnel's hostname was looked up locally before Cloudflare published it and the ISP resolver cached NXDOMAIN for ~28 minutes; the connector now holds a new hostname back for four seconds before saying it.
claude.ai's Add dialog offers no URL edit; ChatGPT's plugin menu offers Edit name/description, Disconnect, Delete — a new hostname means remove and re-add on both, and one more consent each.

ChatGPT annotates every tool `open world, destructive, output schema recommended` and asks Allow once per call because the tools carry no MCP annotations; adding readOnlyHint/destructiveHint would let its `Allow low-risk actions` default apply.

A connector added to a Claude account appears in every Claude surface of that account, including this Claude Code session, as the browser agent's tools; the connector's instructions now say not to use them from a session that has its own.
limits: The service points at a copy of the release binary under ~/.agentdocker/connector/bin until the installed desktop ships `connector`; then `agentdocker connector install` from the installed CLI replaces it.
A quick tunnel's hostname changes at every service start; a named tunnel needs a Cloudflare account and domain the person does not have yet.
ChatGPT's egress was admitted through its published feed as of 2026-09-18; the feed changes and must be refreshed.

inbound_acceptance.result: Passed: a terminal session (claude-code-74334) sent message a67a2614879f4ca3 to claude-browser-qhip through the daemon; in a claude.ai chat, the browser Claude called read_inbox through the connector service, returned that message and ChatGPT's keel broadcast 6deffabefa5f4fcc (a browser agent is a member of the project it joined, so a project broadcast reaches it too), acknowledged both with acknowledge_messages (two Allow-once prompts), and the daemon's inbox for claude-browser-qhip was empty afterwards. The inbound path is cooperative: nothing woke the browser agent; the person's prompt led it to read.
